To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
brassinolide inhibits inwardly rectifying potassium currents of guard cell protoplast and modulates stomatal aperture in Vicia faba.
brassinolide inhibits stomatal opening, and promotes stomatal closure, and that it inhibits the inwardly rectifying potassium current of guard cell protoplast membranes.
brassinosteroids modulate guard cell function and stomatal aperture and that brassinolide and abscisic Acid act synergistically to control ion channels and stomatal movement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms underlying plant hormone regulation of guard cell ion transport and stomatal movement.
the identification of the molecular components of BR signaling and the characterization of their role in the control of plant growth and development.
elucidating the role of BRs in plant physiology and the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of BRs on plant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BRs are able to modulate guard cell physiology, including the control of ion channels, but that they do not act in a manner opposite to ABA.
the effect of BL on stomatal movement was opposite that of ABA, and that BL, like ABA, inhibited the inwardly rectifying potassium current.
the effects of brassinolides on stomatal movement and ion currents are not antagonistic to those of ABA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of brassinosteroid on guard cell is to inhibit K+ channel and thus to induce stomatal closure.
BL, in addition to promoting growth and development of plants, also regulates stomatal movement and guard cell ion channels in a manner that opposes ABA.
BRs are involved in stomatal movement and guard cell physiology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of BRs on guard cell physiology and stomatal aperture are different from other plant systems.
BRs, like ABA, can modulate ion channel activity, which is a key step in stomatal movement.
BRs are not antagonists of ABA action on guard cells.
